Read the answers of a study's requests, check them, write the report files

Source: R/ai_requests.R
tfl_ai_collect_answers.Rd

Reads each <request>.md in answers (the AI's whole answer to the request of the same name, tfl_ai_write_requests()), checks it against its request (tfl_ai_parse(), tfl_ai_check()) and, when it has no error, writes its report files (tfl_ai_unpack()). An answer with errors writes no file: its repair prompt (tfl_ai_repair_prompt()) goes to repairs, to paste into the same chat; save the new answer over the old and collect again.

Usage

tfl_ai_collect_answers(
  study_dir,
  requests = file.path("ai", "requests"),
  answers = file.path("ai", "answers"),
  repairs = file.path("ai", "repairs"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)

Arguments

study_dir

The study folder.

requests, answers, repairs

The folders, under study_dir.

overwrite

TRUE (default) to write over report files already there: an answer collected again replaces its reports.

Value

A tfl_ai_collected: a list with reports (a data frame, one row a report: request, output_id, status – ok, warning, error, no answer –, problems (how many), first (the first problem), problems_text (all of them, one a line), file (the report's spec/outputs/<id>.yml when written, else NA), repair (the request's repair prompt to paste into the same chat, else NA)), next_steps (a request's next step, named by the request), assumptions (the study's spec/_assumptions.yml for these reports: output_id, where, item, assumption, question), stray (answer files named after no request), requests (the requests' folder), templates (each request's setting, tfl_ai_prepare()'s templates: a logical named by the request), manifest and manifest_file (below).

The manifest is every report the answers say they make, for the person to check the count against the TOC (one TOC row can be several reports): each answer lists its reports first (reports:, one line a report: id, title, split – how its TOC row is split for it –, toc – the TOC row's number). A data frame, one row a report: request, toc, output_id, title, split, listed (FALSE: a report the answer writes but does not list; NA: a request not answered or not read, its reports as asked) and status (the report's, as in reports, or "not answered": listed, but no report file in the answer). It is written to ai/manifest.csv (UTF-8) beside the requests' folder, anew at each collection. The paths are relative to study_dir. Its print is a summary: each request's status, its reports and the next step.

Details

An answer is read as UTF-8, with or without the byte-order mark Windows Notepad writes, and with any line ends; an answer saved in another encoding (Shift-JIS / CP932, "ANSI") is an error that says how to save it again. An answer saved as <request>.md.txt or <request>.txt (Notepad adds .txt) is read too.

See also

tfl_ai_write_requests()
